title: Protocol to dissociate healthy and infected murine- and hamster-derived lung tissue for single-cell transcriptome analysis
protocol: Subject laboratory animals to deep anesthesia according to approved protocols.
Confirm depth of anesthesia by loss of pedal withdrawal reflex.
Sacrifice animals by bleeding out via heat puncture.
Collect EDTA blood and place it on ice if required for analysis.
Collect clotting tubes separately and allow clotting at 20°C if required for analysis.
Place anesthetized animals in a secured supine position.
Soak abdominal and thoracic areas with 70% ethanol to disinfect the fur.
Open the abdominal cavity by incising the abdominal skin and peritoneum from the sternum to the pubis using surgical scissors and forceps.
Sacrifice the animal by bleeding out through transection of the abdominal vena cava if not done previously.
Collect blood or serum from the abdominal vena cava in a 1 mL syringe for analysis, if needed.
Open the thoracic cavity and expose the heart and lungs.
Perfuse the pulmonary vessels through the animals’ right heart ventricle by slowly flushing with 5 mL lung perfusion medium using a 5 mL syringe capped with a 26G needle.
Lift up the lungs by pulling the trachea.
Dissect the lungs free from surrounding tissues.
Dip the lungs twice into ice-cold PBS to remove residual fluid or blood.
Remove the trachea.
Place the lungs (for mice) or right caudal lobe (for hamsters) in an individual well of a 6-well plate or in an individual petri dish.
Add 2 mL lung digestion medium.
Clean forceps with 1× PBS.
Place lungs into 3 mL RPMI medium or PBS containing 1% BSA and 2 μg/mL actinomycin D on ice until all animals are dissected.

Mechanically dissociate the tissue by securing it with straight anatomical forceps in one hand and repeatedly hitting it with a second curved anatomical set of forceps held in the other hand for approximately 2–3 min.
Incubate lung tissue at 37°C with occasional shaking for 30 min.
Add 8 mL ice-cold 1% BSA/PBS buffer to stop enzymatic digestion.
Pipette the tissue and liquid up and down 3–10 times using a 5 mL serological pipette.
Collect the complete suspension in a 10 mL serological pipette and discharge onto a 70 μm cell strainer placed on top of a 50 mL conical tube.
Use the plunger of a 5 mL syringe to gently swipe remaining lung tissue through the cell strainer.
Rinse the well with 10 mL cold 1% BSA/PBS or 0.5% BSA/PBS buffer and pass it through the cell strainer.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Add RBC lysis buffer (2–10 mL) to the cell pellet and carefully resuspend.
Incubate the suspension for 2–5 min at 20°C.
Determine the appropriate volume and incubation time for RBC lysis based on rodent species and experimental settings.
Incubate cell suspension with RBC lysis buffer for an appropriate duration to achieve effective RBC lysis.
Stop RBC lysis by adding at least 10 mL of 0.04% BSA/PBS buffer.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 6 min at 4°C and discard the supernatant.
Check if the pellet has turned colorless to ensure complete RBC lysis; repeat steps if necessary.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 4-10 mL of 0.04% BSA/PBS buffer.
Filter the single cell suspension through a 40 μm cell strainer placed on top of a 15 mL conical tube.
Dilute the single cell suspension 1:10 in trypan blue solution by adding 20 μL cell suspension to 180 μL trypan blue solution.
Gently pipette to mix and allow for counting cells using a Neubauer hemocytometer.
Count cells in the 4 square subdivisions placed at the corners of a Neubauer hemocytometer (S1 – S4).
Calculate the cell concentration for each sample using the formula: cell count = (S1 + S2 + S3 + S4) / 4 x dilution factor x 10,000 x sample volume [mL].
Visually check cell viability and singularity on the hemocytometer.
Adjust the single cell suspension to approximately 500 μL to 1 mL with an appropriate concentration for single-cell RNA-sequencing by diluting with 0.04% BSA/PBS buffer.
Filter 500 μL to 1 mL of the diluted suspension with Flowmi® cell strainers (40 μm) to remove cell clumps.
